name: HubSpot

auth_methods: Scoped Service Keys (public beta) for system-to-system access
Legacy private-app access tokens remain available
OAuth 2.1 with PKCE for the remote CRM MCP connector
findings.api_type: REST APIs, webhooks and official remote MCP
findings.api_breadth: Broad CRM objects, associations, activities, marketing/content, files, automation and account APIs. Remote MCP supports selected CRM/activity/content/marketing reads and writes, with object, subscription, beta and permission restrictions.

evidence.title: Developer Platform Basics & Onboarding
evidence.excerpt: Developers can start with a free HubSpot account; platform building blocks include REST APIs, OAuth, webhooks and MCP.

evidence.title: Service Keys enter public beta
evidence.excerpt: Service Keys are scoped account-level credentials for internal system integrations, require Developer Tools permissions and do not support webhooks; legacy private apps remain available.

evidence.title: 2026-09 API reference
evidence.excerpt: Current reference covers CRM, content, conversations, automation, files, events, marketing, revenue and account resources.

evidence.title: Integrate AI tools with the HubSpot MCP server
evidence.excerpt: CRM MCP uses a connector and OAuth with PKCE; current tools include selected CRM, activity, content, campaign and social writes, with subscription/beta and user-permission gates.

notes: Independent findings were frozen before reading first_pass.json. Verdict covers a reusable integration: a free scoped prototype is feasible, while premium resources and some MCP operations have additional gates. The remote CRM MCP is distinct from the developer MCP. Current guide says Sensitive Data blocks conversation data; an older April announcement described a broader Activity block, so do not treat that announcement as the complete current scope.

name: DealCloud

auth_methods: REST: OAuth 2 client credentials using client ID and API key, exchanged for a short-lived Bearer token
findings.api_type: REST APIs with OpenAPI/Swagger; official DealCloud MCP
findings.api_breadth: REST includes schema, data read/create/update/upsert/delete, user management, backups, publications/events and relationship-intelligence imports. MCP can explore schema, query/read data and optionally create/update records, with write tools enabled separately.

evidence.title: DealCloud API Docs
evidence.excerpt: Documents REST functional areas for schema, data, users, backups, events/publications and relationship intelligence, with a site-specific Swagger/OpenAPI specification.

evidence.title: Obtaining an API Key
evidence.excerpt: An admin enables API capability on the user's group; permitted users then enable/copy their API key in Profile. Admin or CSM help is needed when permission is absent.

evidence.title: Requesting an OAuth2 Bearer Token
evidence.excerpt: REST uses client credentials with client ID/API key and required scopes; Bearer tokens expire after 15 minutes and are reissued by repeating the flow.

evidence.title: Getting Started with DealCloud MCP
evidence.excerpt: MCP requires a DealCloud with Celeste license, admin Manage MCP Servers capability, and Celeste Member plus MCP Access for end users.

evidence.title: DealCloud MCP Authentication
evidence.excerpt: MCP uses OAuth on behalf of the signed-in user and inherits that user's object, field and record permissions.

evidence.title: MCP Tools
evidence.excerpt: MCP offers schema discovery, lookups/search/query and record create/update; an administrator must switch on Enable Write Tools.

notes: REST feasibility is conditional on an existing licensed site and group/API permissions. No universal free sandbox or trial was established. MCP has a specific Celeste license and separate enablement gate; an API key alone does not establish MCP access. Independent findings frozen before comparison.

name: Zendesk

auth_methods: OAuth 2 authorization code, with PKCE for public clients
OAuth 2 client credentials for server integrations
Legacy email/token Basic authentication (deprecated; OAuth migration required)
findings.api_type: HTTPS REST APIs and official MCP via Zendesk Bridge EAP
findings.api_breadth: Support account operations include tickets, users/organizations and help-center resources; the MCP EAP exposes assigned tools such as ticket create/update, user lookup, help-center search and macros, with governed connection permissions.

evidence.title: Security and authentication
evidence.excerpt: Current guide recommends OAuth, labels API tokens deprecated, requires verified users, and requires global OAuth for multi-customer distribution rather than collecting customer credentials.

evidence.title: Using OAuth to authenticate API requests
evidence.excerpt: Documents authorization-code and client-credentials flows, inherited user permissions, refresh behavior and administrator setup of OAuth clients.

evidence.title: Connecting external AI agents to Zendesk MCP or Zendesk AI agents (EAP)
evidence.excerpt: Vendor MCP/Bridge is an EAP requiring participation; admins assign tools to a connection, and documented actions include tickets, users, organizations, help-center search and macros.

evidence.title: Zendesk Pricing
evidence.excerpt: Provides a trial route and paid support plans; enterprise entitlements and sandbox availability vary by plan.

notes: API tokens remain described as a deprecated legacy route, so new integration design should use OAuth. Internal and distributed multi-customer integrations have different OAuth requirements. MCP EAP availability must not be generalized to every account. Independent findings frozen before comparison; no login/API calls.

name: Gladly

auth_methods: REST HTTP Basic: agent email as username and API token as password
Gladly MCP for Claude: each person's Gladly sign-in, without shared API tokens
findings.api_type: HTTPS REST/JSON API, Lookup API and webhooks; official inbound MCP for Gladly AI
findings.api_breadth: REST covers customer profiles, customer timelines/conversations, agents and webhooks, while the Lookup API is called by Gladly against the customer's service. Inbound MCP focuses on AI session analysis, Guides/Workflows/Actions/Knowledge and Simulator testing rather than an asserted mirror of the complete REST API.

evidence.title: Gladly API
evidence.excerpt: Organization REST API exchanges JSON over HTTPS with agent-email/API-token Basic auth; admins assign API User permission. Also documents Lookup services, sandbox enablement and event webhooks.

evidence.title: Get Your API tokens
evidence.excerpt: Users with API User role create credentials in the Gladly UI under App Developer Tools.

evidence.title: What is the Gladly MCP for Claude?
evidence.excerpt: Inbound MCP for Claude works on AI sessions and AI configuration/testing, and requires closed-beta organization enablement, an eligible role and paid Claude access. It is separate from Gladly calling external MCP servers.

evidence.title: Review security and data for Gladly MCP
evidence.excerpt: Each person connects with Gladly sign-in; MCP follows role permissions and has no shared API keys.

evidence.title: Invoice and Billing Overview
evidence.excerpt: Gladly subscriptions and licenses are billed under agreed order-form/contract terms; this is not evidence of a self-serve free API account.

notes: Product naming changed: former Hero platform is Gladly Team, while Sidekick is Gladly AI. REST and inbound MCP target related but different surfaces. Closed-beta MCP requires vendor enablement; an existing tenant can still implement the documented REST route once an admin grants API User. No general free developer account was established. Independent findings frozen before comparison.

name: Lark (Larksuite)

auth_methods: App ID/App Secret to obtain app/tenant access tokens
OAuth 2.0 user access tokens for user-context APIs and local MCP
findings.api_type: HTTPS Open APIs and events; official locally run OpenAPI MCP
findings.api_breadth: Broad app capabilities around messages/chats, documents, calendars, Base and contacts, limited by the chosen tool preset, scopes, resource permissions and identity. The official MCP README explicitly excludes file upload/download and direct cloud-document editing in that implementation.

evidence.title: Official Lark OpenAPI MCP repository
evidence.excerpt: Official beta MCP runs with app credentials and optional OAuth user sign-in. It supports selected API tools/presets, requires the international domain for Lark, and lists file-transfer/document-edit limitations.

evidence.title: General parameters
evidence.excerpt: Official indexed terminology distinguishes app_access_token, tenant_access_token and user_access_token for app, organization and user authority.

evidence.title: Custom app development process
evidence.excerpt: Official indexed guide allows organization creation through a Free Trial route; custom apps need tenant-admin approval for production, with test companies/users supporting development before release.

evidence.title: Apply for API permissions
evidence.excerpt: Custom scopes may be auto-approved or require tenant review; store apps require platform-launch and tenant-installation review. Development exceptions do not imply production approval.

notes: Direct Lark doc opens rendered shells; cited indexed official text and the readable vendor-owned repository were independently reviewed. Remote-MCP setup documentation is marked Deprecated and described internal testing, so it is not used to promise generally available hosted access. Local official MCP exists; vendor_official does not imply every hosted variant is current. Feishu China and international Lark domains/app identities are distinct. Independent findings frozen before comparison.

name: Pumble

auth_methods: Generated API key for the API addon
MCP: user or bot token plus app key in token and x-app-token headers
findings.api_type: HTTPS API addon and official remote HTTP MCP
findings.api_breadth: API addon handles messages/replies/deletion/reactions/channel creation and selected channel/message listings. MCP dynamically exposes scope-approved tools including message search/read/send/edit, scheduling, channel/user/workspace information and file fetching.

evidence.title: Pumble API Overview
evidence.excerpt: API addon is available to Owner/Admin/Member on all plans; install it, allow permissions and generate an API key. Documented actions include messaging, reactions, channels and selected listings.

evidence.title: How to use the Pumble MCP server
evidence.excerpt: Vendor HTTP MCP at mcp.pumble.com/mcp uses a created/installed app's user/bot token plus app key; tools are dynamically limited to selected user/bot scopes.

evidence.title: Pumble Plans & Pricing
evidence.excerpt: Free workspace plan is available with a finite number of app/integration slots; paid plans raise integration limits.

notes: API addon and custom-app MCP credentials are distinct. Build-now refers to a scoped own-workspace API prototype after installation/permission grant. Private-channel message listing needs the addon bot in that channel. Exact current custom-app entitlement should be checked against workspace settings; no credentials or API calls were used. Independent findings frozen before comparison.
